title: Honeybee hives and oilseed rape crops in combination mitigated the negative impacts of honeybee spillover on plant reproduction in alpine meadows
content:
During bloom, mass-flowering crops can mitigate the otherwise negative impacts of hive introductions on plant reproduction by improving niche partitioning among wild pollinators. This study improves our understanding of the context-dependent responses of natural plant–pollinator communities to the introduction of hives in agricultural landscapes and provides a framework for optimized agricultural planning in high-altitude ecosystems that balance food production with biodiversity conservation.


Abstract

The global expansion of agriculture, particularly the cultivation of mass-flowering crops and the introduction of industrial-scale beekeeping, threatens biodiversity by disrupting plant–pollinator interactions in natural communities. A deeper understanding of their individual and combined impacts and the spatial aspect of these impacts is urgently needed to mitigate their impacts on natural communities. Here, we investigated whether and how introducing managed honeybees (Apis mellifera L.) and oilseed rape (OSR) (Brassica rapa var. oleifera), individually and in combination, impacts natural plant–pollinator communities in Tibetan alpine meadows during crop flowering. Specifically, we studied 18 pairs of meadow sites subjected to two sets of treatments: First, agricultural introduction treatment with three levels (i.e. hives, OSR crop or both combined were introduced in the area), and second, the distance of focal meadows to hives and/or crop edges (near plot <50 m; and far plot ~700 m). Independent of introduction treatment, honeybees visited plants more frequently (2.52 times) in near plots than in far plots, indicating proximity to hives and/or crop edges resulted in honeybee spillover into adjacent meadows. The spillover of honeybees had negative impacts on the reproduction of wild plants, such that in meadows with hives or crops only, proximity to either hives or crop edges resulted in a general decrease in seed set of wild plants. However, in meadows with both hives and crops, the seed set was similar between near and far plots, indicating that oilseed crops and hives in combination mitigated the negative impacts of honeybee spillover. Further analysis suggested that this mitigation was associated with a higher complementary specialization of wild pollinators in crop + hive meadows. Synthesis and applications. During bloom, mass-flowering crops can mitigate the otherwise negative impacts of hive introductions on plant reproduction by improving niche partitioning among wild pollinators. This study improves our understanding of the context-dependent responses of natural plant–pollinator communities to the introduction of hives in agricultural landscapes and provides a framework for optimized agricultural planning in high-altitude ecosystems that balance food production with biodiversity conservation.

摘要

伴随全球农业扩张，大量引入集约化种植(养殖)的开花作物和传粉者会影响破坏自然生境中的植物-传粉者互作，危及生物多样性。深入理解开花作物和人工养殖传粉者各自的生态影响及其复合效应有助于制定管理方案以减轻集约化农业生产对自然群落的影响。 本研究探讨了在青藏高原高寒草甸中，分别和同时引入人工饲养蜜蜂(Apis mellifera)与油菜(Brassica rapa var. oleifera)对植物-传粉者网络及植物繁殖的影响。我们选取了18对高寒草甸样点，分属两种因素的处理:农业物种引入处理(包含三个水平:仅引入蜂箱、仅种植油菜、两者同时引入)；距引入物种的不同距离(包含两个水平:靠近引入物种-50米以内、远离引入物种-约700米)。 结果显示，蜜蜂的访花频率在三种引入处理间没有显著差异，但在近距离样地中显著高于远距离样地(2.52倍)，表明蜂箱和油菜花田均对临近草甸造成了蜜蜂溢出效应。蜜蜂的溢出对草甸植物的繁殖造成了负面影响，以至于在仅存在蜂箱或油菜花田的样点中，靠近蜂箱/油菜花田的样地中植物的结子率显著降低。然而，在同时存在蜂箱与油菜花田的样地中，植物的结子率在远、近样地间没有显著差异，表明同时引入蜂箱与油菜花田减轻了蜜蜂溢出的负面影响。进一步的分析表明产生这一效应的原因是在蜂箱+油菜花田样点中野生传粉者的觅食特化程度较高。 这些结果表明，协同引入开花作物与人工养殖蜜蜂可通过增强传粉者间的生态位分化来减轻蜜蜂溢出的生态影响。本研究有助于深化对多种人工管理物种引入情况下生物多样性格局与生态过程的理解，并为高海拔生态系统中兼顾农业生产与生物多样性保护的管理规划提供了科学依据。
